title: Spark ignores timezone of a timestamp
question:
I have tried to load to a spark data frame but seems like it ignores the timezone of a timestamp and uses spark timezone instead. Here is a code to run it.

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, Row
from datetime import datetime
import pytz
import os
spark = SparkSession.builder.getOrCreate()
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.session.timeZone", "Europe/Moscow")
df = spark.createDataFrame([
       Row(user_id = 'user_id', time=pytz.timezone("UTC").localize(datetime.combine(datetime(2020, 1, 1), datetime.min.time())))
    ])
for row in df.collect():
    print(row['time'])
    print(pytz.timezone("UTC").localize(datetime.combine(datetime(2020, 1, 1), datetime.min.time())))
df.show()

Here is the output in this case

2020-01-01 03:00:00                                                             
2020-01-01 00:00:00+00:00
+-------+-------------------+
|user_id|               time|
+-------+-------------------+
|user_id|2020-01-01 03:00:00|
+-------+-------------------+

Could you please tell me if it's expected behavior?
answer:
Spark respects the zoneid set in the configuration. Here are some examples to understand.

+05:30 => My timezone i.e Asia/Calcutta

+05:00 => Pakistan

+03:00 => Moscow

Using default timezone or systemtem timezone ( here +05:30 for India )

println(java.time.ZoneId.systemDefault.toString)
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.session.timeZone", java.time.ZoneId.systemDefault.toString)
spark.sql("""
select id, cast('2020-01-01 00:00:00+00:00' as timestamp) ts from range(1) 
""").show(false)

Asia/Calcutta
+---+-------------------+
|id |ts                 |
+---+-------------------+
|0  |2020-01-01 05:30:00|  //Midnight in London is morning 5:30 in India
+---+-------------------+

Cast a timestamp that is having Pakistan zone info

spark.conf.set("spark.sql.session.timeZone", java.time.ZoneId.systemDefault.toString)
spark.sql("""
select id, cast('2020-01-01 00:00:00+05:00' as timestamp) ts from range(1) 
""").show(false)
+---+-------------------+
|id |ts                 |
+---+-------------------+
|0  |2020-01-01 00:30:00| //Pakistan midnight is 30 mins past midnight in India
+---+-------------------+

Now change the setting to "Europe/Moscow"

spark.conf.set("spark.sql.session.timeZone", "Europe/Moscow")
spark.sql("""
select id, cast('2020-01-01 00:00:00+00:00' as timestamp) ts from range(1) 
""").show(false)


+---+-------------------+
|id |ts                 |
+---+-------------------+
|0  |2020-01-01 03:00:00| //Midnight in London is 3 hrs past in Moscow
+---+-------------------+

Another example:

spark.conf.set("spark.sql.session.timeZone", "Europe/Moscow")
spark.sql("""
select id, cast('2020-01-01 00:00:00+05:00' as timestamp) ts from range(1) 
""").show(false)

+---+-------------------+
|id |ts                 |
+---+-------------------+
|0  |2019-12-31 22:00:00| // Midnight in Pakistan is 2 hrs away for Moscow.
+---+-------------------+

Note: If there is no zoneinfo, simply the "datetime" part is attached to the zoneid configured.

spark.conf.set("spark.sql.session.timeZone", "Europe/Moscow")
spark.sql("""
select id, cast('2020-01-01 00:00:00' as timestamp) ts from range(1) 
""").show(false)
+---+-------------------+
|id |ts                 |
+---+-------------------+
|0  |2020-01-01 00:00:00|
+---+-------------------+
